scope: classify and correct OCR106-ACL-001 catalog fixture execution authority

decisions.evidence: With postgres changed to NOSUPERUSER and unable to SET privacy_workflow_owner, the original GRANT emits no privileges were granted; wrapper proacl is byte-identical before and after, and the old held assertion fails. The failed PG17.6 run therefore did not prove a source ACL-seal gap.

An artificially injected privacy_workflow_owner default EXECUTE grant can reproduce the symptom locally, but the PG17.6 read-only catalog event reports no such creator default ACL. This experiment is not used as the root-cause conclusion.

When the wrapper owner actually grants an explicit supabase_admin ACL item and proacl readback confirms it, the existing exact function_contract comparison returns held. Migration, compiler, manifest, durable source, and application tests remain byte-identical to the prior accepted freeze.

The fixture creates a savepoint-scoped postgres-granted SET=true owner lease, changes role to privacy_workflow_owner, performs the GRANT, asserts the explicit proacl item exists, and only then requires capability held. Each savepoint rollback removes the lease and mutation.

Both owner-drift cases now create the same bounded owner lease and assert relowner actually changed. For catalog-table owner drift, the new owner grants postgres SELECT so the SECURITY DEFINER capability can read the contract and directly return held; rollback restores owner, ACL, schema grant, and membership.

verification.command: PG17.11 synthetic harness with postgres NOSUPERUSER and original non-owner GRANT probe
verification.result: expected failure: warning no privileges were granted; baseline and post-GRANT proacl identical; old held assertion fails

verification.command: PG17.11 synthetic harness with supabase_admin SUPERUSER but an actual explicit owner-authorized GRANT
verification.result: explicit supabase_admin proacl item observed; capability held; full fixture passed
exit 0; catalog fixture and durable release fixture passed
exit 0; catalog fixture passed with postgres NOSUPERUSER; terminal membership restored to ADMIN=true, INHERIT=false, SET=false, grantor=supabase_admin

limits: The NOSUPERUSER reproduction is a disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 synthetic harness; the corrected fixture still requires a fresh PostgreSQL 17.6 full-catalog rerun by the integration owner.
The catalog-table owner mutation intentionally preserves the capability definer minimum SELECT access, so it tests a real owner-plus-ACL drift while retaining direct JSON held readback.
Application TypeScript, migration identity, compiler, manifest, quota semantics, and provider paths were unchanged; app build/parity and the prior 32-pass suite were not repeated.
